en: The *Indrasahasranāmastotra* is the composition of Gaṇapati.
Indra is the most divine deity, the non-blue one, the fair-winged, whose chariot-seat is full;
he is the subduer of all, the lord of all, and the observer of all people. || 1 ||
The doer of all things, higher than all, the source of all, the vast one— conscious and existing by his own power, he is beyond, without wheels.
Viśvānara, Viśvarūpa, Viśvāyu, Viśvataspṛthu, Viśvakarman, Viśvadeva—by him, the wise one, all things are fashioned on every side. || 3 ||
Born in the three worlds, the sharp-horned god, the ruddy sun moving as a red-hot blaze,
the supreme wise one, shining and making the lightless shine, is unborn.
The eldest of men, the bull, the light, the greatest in power and greatness; the subduer of those with hostile intentions, the upholder of every sacred rite. (5)
The upholder of riches, the creator of creators, the steadfast one impelled by wisdom;
the means of accomplishing the sacrifice, the sacrifice itself, the bearer of the sacrifice, and the first-born of the waters.
Delighting in the sacrifice, worthy of worship, he who has harnessed the pressing-stones and is swift in his aid;
possessing a good thunderbolt, the shaker, the warrior, glorious, worthy of sacrifice, and mighty. || 7 ||
He is the repeller of the evil-minded, the slayer of the wicked Rākṣasa,
the impeller of the emaciated, the performer of deeds, the creator of sacred knowledge, and one whose vows are steadfast.
Possessing firm vigor, the protector of prayers, the gatherer of riches, the unshakable, the destroyer of darkness, the fashioner, the guardian of the body, and the savior of the distressed. (9)
He of brilliant valor, of brilliant aspect, the subduer of the swift, the unconquered;
he who increased the Tugrya, the most bountiful, the one of many heroic deeds, the impetuous.
The bull-like one of radiant luster, the knower of all things, whose wrath is fierce yet who is praised;
the joyous leader of hymns, the bull accompanied by the Maruts, the seer of the Maruts. 11.
The great-handed Gaṇapati, the inspirer of the intellect, Bṛhaspati; the mighty one, the giver of joy, the exhilarating one, Marka, Arka, the wise one, the great. 12.
Thus ends the first hundred names.
He is the one who conforms to all forms, the supreme measure, the one of many forms, the one praised by many;
he is invoked by many, the one who stands before all, the one of manifold illusions, and the destroyer of citadels. || 13 ||
Praised by many, performing much, the shatterer of forts, most abundant; much-lauded, the victor in battles, of many forms, the shaker. 14.
The filler, the wise one, the encompasser, the most praiseworthy, the unopposed;
the fully grown, the long-lived, the protector, accompanied by Pūṣan, the bringer of what is within reach. 15.
Puruṣāka, Pāñcajanya, Purubhoja, Puruvasu, Piśaṅgarāti, Papuri, Puroyodha, and Pṛthujrayas. 16.

From of old, he is the ancient one, the one who was before, the first-born seer; the leader, the wise counselor, the praiseworthy one who travels the ancient path, the possessor of abundant wealth. 17.

The one who offers first oblations, the purifier, Pūṣan, the tracker of paths, the maker of ways, the lord, the one who wards off many, the gray-haired, the impeller, the sender, the protector, and the father. || 18 ||
Possessing abundant manly vigor, established upon the mountains, with his wrath directed forward, he is the one placed at the forefront;
the shatterer of fortresses, unassailable, born of old, and most far-extending. 19.
The conqueror of armies, powerful of arm, raising great dust, unrestrained, the overcomer with iron weapons, possessing a vast covering. 20.
Beloved by Brahman, impelled by Brahman, borne by Brahman, reaching the goal;
with a mind set on awakening, straightening the crooked, possessing great radiance, and slaying the enemies. 21.

Performing many deeds, a doer of great works in battle, a bringer of blessings, a sustainer of the earth, a bearer of burdens—he who is to be invoked in battles, possessed of abundant vigor, the slayer of fortresses, the swift victor. 22.
The breaker of hosts, the terrible buffalo, the destroyer of many sons and of curses;
the one who looks upon all, the lord of the people, the hero, the protector from enemies, the lord of the dead. 23.
Thus ends the second hundred names.
Most bountiful, most fatherly, rich in food, Bhṛgu, Paṇi;
the one who has looked upon us, the destroyer of forts, the seeker of water, the slayer of the arrogant foe. 24.
The ancient bull of the earth, the exhilarating one, the first and broad; he who is as expansive as the ocean, the protector, the beacon, the subduer of men. 25.
The sustainer of the singer, the increaser of the poet, the youthful one, the possessor of wisdom, the wisdom itself;
dwelling in the night, the most wise, borne by songs, the impeller of the praiser. 26.
Kṣapāvān, Kauśika, Kārī, Rājā, Akṣamya, Gopati;
Gauḥ, Gorduraḥ, Duro’ścasya, Yavasyaduraḥ, Āduriḥ. || 27 ||
Candrabudhna, Carṣaṇiprā, Cakṛtya, Codayanmati, Candrabhānu, Citratama, Camrīṣa, and Cakramāsaja. || 28 ||
Possessing much strength, possessing great splendor, possessing many progeny, and possessing great exhilaration;
possessing great action, possessing great friction, possessing great pervasion, and possessing great protection. 29.
Possessing great manliness, great neck, great wealth, and great wisdom;
of great measure, great grasp, great bounty, and great resonance. || 30 ||

The impetuous one, the praised, the one who bestows much, the one who is swift to act, the one who grants abundance, the one who stands upon the chariot, the one who carries across, the exultant, the radiant, and the unshakable. 31.
Destroying the fear of the trembling with his power, he is powerful,
swift, a crosser, a conqueror, a protector, impetuous, rapid, and the most excellent of the strong.
He who has grown through sacrifice, the foremost among those worthy of sacrifice, the increaser of the sacrificer;
the devourer of enemies, the unblinking, the manifold, the ageless one who does not favor those who do not press the soma.

He whose protection is imperishable, who is invincible, noble, possessing beautiful cheeks, and who has mounted upon the bull; he whose ears hear all, who fills the mid-air, who possesses immeasurable power, and who is praised by the enemy.
Thus ends the third hundred of names.
The unseen, sole sovereign, the one above, whose dwelling is on high, ancient yet ever-youthful;
steadfast, the sun, whose power is his own majesty, whose gifts are truth, and who is renowned from of old. || 35 ||
The ordainer of beings, the banner, the one who never falls from his station, the far-reaching; the lord of power, self-born, possessed of might, he who is never seen to falter.
He whose vigor is truth, whose being is truth, the son of Truth, the drinker of Soma;
the slayer of the Dasyu, the upholder of heaven, the king, and the conscious essence of the celestial realm. (37)
Worthy of praise, swift-moving, radiant, bestowing strength, protector of cosmic order, himself the cosmic order;
possessor of the soma-residue, creator of joy, divine, following the seasons, and impeller of the weak. 38.
The one who is the leader among the seers, the protector of the earth, the king, the abode of wealth, the bestower of riches;
the lord of the *Ṛbhus*, the immeasurable, the swift horse, the conqueror, he who belongs to the ocean. (39)

The one who brings forth the debt, the mountain-like, the one whose color is like a mountain, the one who is active, the one who strikes down the obstructors, the one who makes the limbs firm, the one who possesses the residue of the soma, the finder of wealth, the one to be invoked, the bold one in battles, the seer. 40.
The one who exults, the firm one, the sage, the knower of all, the increaser of Truth;
he who yokes the Truth, the performer of Dharma, the milch-cow, the winner of wealth, the bearer of light, and the wearer of armor. 41.
Born of Truth, the victorious, the one worthy of Soma, the conqueror of assemblies, the steadfast;
seeking Truth, the powerful, the enduring, borne by the thunderbolt, equal to the Rigveda. 42.
He is the singer of hymns, the unassailable, the one of impetuous vigor, the excellent guardian, and the most self-glorious;
he possesses the best aid and grace, is victorious, provides good guidance, performs righteous deeds, and is pure. 42.
The son of strength, the bounteous one, the Vasu accompanied by his host, worthy of praise, the winner of all, the ever-conquering, the bearer of hymns, the subduer of enemies. 44.
Thus ends the fourth hundred of names.

Most powerful, son of strength, possessing a hundredfold wrath and a hundredfold wisdom, Śakra, the one who aids men, the impetuous, whose ears hear, and the friend who makes his companions famous. 45.
Possessing a hundredfold protection, bold in leadership, providing a hundredfold guidance, and possessing a hundredfold wealth;
he is the one who proclaims the hymn, the most auspicious, who bears a name worthy of being heard, and who is never bowed down.

The hero, with beautiful jaws, possessing thousandfold aid, the radiant one, the bull with curved horns, the son of the waters, the ruler, the powerful, desiring glory, endowed with strength, the slayer of the enemy. 47.
The Lord who fashions beautiful forms, the one who grows great, the husband of Śacī; he whose essence is truth, the winner of prizes, the possessor of power, and the one of immeasurable resolve.

Possessing a thousandfold wisdom, well-disposed, worthy of hearing, pure, whose wealth is sacred learning, the invoker at the sacrificial session, the drinker of Soma, of noble will, he rests upon his beard.
Increased by the *codas*, he is the lord of all that breathes in the world; the son of the *Citra* (the Shining One), possessing excellent hands, moving forward, and ever-increasing. 50.

He is the one who fulfills his own desire, the true lord of the virtuous, the truthful, the beautiful, the most heroic, the swift, the wonderful, the wise, the knower, and the standard of comparison for every being. 51.

He is the steadfast one, the conscious one, the true friend, the one of wondrous deeds, the most renowned, the one who bestows strength, the one well-heard of, the sovereign ruler, the one easy to cross over, and the friend of the one who presses the soma. 52.
Brahmavāhas, Tamas, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Vasva, Pati, Hari, Rudra prepared for battle, Raṇiteśa, Kṛt, and Śiva. || 53 ||
Impelled by wisdom, most wise, the mighty wielder of the golden thunderbolt, the enclosure, the most heroic hero, Vāyu, Mātariśvan, the friend of the Maruts. 54.
He of celebrated fame, praised by all, who hears our invocation, the far-seeing one;
the showerer of blessings, the lord of wealth, the vigorous, the bull, the possessor of strength and riches. 55.
Thus ends the fifth hundred [of names].
Vigra, Vibhīṣaṇa, Vahni, Vṛddhāyu, Viśruta, Vṛṣa, Vrajabhṛt, Vṛtrahā, Vṛddha, Viśvavāra, and Vṛtañcaya. || 56 ||
He whose impulse is virile, whose chariot is virile, whose gifts are virile, whose will is virile;
he whose deeds are virile, whose mind is virile, most skillful, the increaser of the one who presses the Soma. 57.

He whose speech is free from deceit, the slayer of Asuras, the wise ordainer, the performer of universal sacrifice, the ageless, the shoreless, the one easily invoked, the fearless, the overcomer of adversaries, and the foremost of the Angirases. || 58 ||

The immortal one, armed with his own weapons, without enemies, unassailable, and the subduer of adversaries; the wise one, the son, the worshipful one, of uniform vision, and the bestower of fearlessness.
The leader whose rays are desirable, the fulfiller of blessings, the unassailable, the winner of light, the creator of prosperity, and the supreme protector of those who praise him. 60.
Ajātaśatru, Senānī, Ubhayāvī, Ubhayaṅkara, Urugāya, Satyayoni, Sahasvān, and Anurvarāpati. || 61 ||
Fierce is the protector, fierce-armed, with a fierce bow;
he who increases the hymns, renowned for his songs, king of chants, profound, and most fond of praise.
The bull among the seekers of the earth, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand; he whose right hand wields the vajra;
the lover of Soma, the lord of Soma, increased by Soma, and most skillful.
Subrahmanya is the elder, the hero, the most powerful, the far-reaching, the sovereign;
he has a golden beard, possesses tawny steeds, is the lord of bay horses, and is invincible. 64.
Golden-armed, far-reaching, golden-haired, golden-bearded; golden-jawed, being desired, born of gold, and the supporter of the golden. || 65 ||
Golden-hued, with bay horses, having a golden form, beloved by the bay ones;
most destructive, with bay-eyed horses, to be invoked, standing upon the bay ones, yoking the bay ones.
Thus ends the sixth hundred of names.
He whose jaw is excellent, who possesses a good realm, who has heroic sons, who is a seer who drinks the pressed juice,
who is the breaker of the enclosure, who carries away the village, and who is the seeker of cattle— [to him] (67).
The victorious one, the lord of all that stands still, the lord of all that moves, the dancer;
the king of men, the leader who knows manly deeds, the impeller of strength. 68.
Pressing forward, the protector of men, the supreme lord of rivers, the manly one with his teams of horses, the well-ordered, the unassailable, and the most difficult to overcome—may he come.
A new deposer, manly-minded, acting in concert, easy to cross over;
most manly, roaring like a bull, most youthful, the most heroic conqueror of men.
Most discerning, with arms like thunderbolts, the devourer of Vṛtra, the breaker of Vala;
wearing golden ornaments, most excellent, the consumer of men, and the subduer of people.

The subduer of all, the bull among cattle, the crusher of the wicked, the destroyer of the impious, the conqueror of men, the breaker of forts, the overcomer of cities, the vanquisher of enemies, the lord of all that moves and stands still. 72.

He who brings together the worlds, he who joins them well, he who perceives clearly, the progenitor, the ruddy one; he who is celestial, he whose luster is self-radiant, the good protector, he who is to be praised, the ancient-born, the seeker of light. || 73 ||
Providing a signal for the signal-less, providing form for the formless;
having struck down the great ones with his thunderbolt, he is the one praised by the Maruts, the one who goes among the Maruts. 74.
The great hero, the great host, the one worthy of great honor, the vast wisdom; the mother of the wealthy ones, most generous, full of spirit, and the most spirited of all. 75.
The ram, the supporter of the earth, exhilarated with pride, possessing greatness, and of great intellect;
the smearer, the healer, most bountiful, performing acts of smearing, and most magnificent. || 76 ||

He who crushes the intoxication of pride, the lord of glories, the heat [of his majesty], the one of excellent praise, the giver of well-being, the seer of heaven, the source of riches, and the lord. 77.
Thus ends the seventh hundred of names.
The arrow-handed one, the giver of arrows, the giver of wealth, the bestower of riches;
the all-pervasive, the destroyer of obstacles, the pure, the most excellent, the conqueror of all, the omnipresent. 78.
Beholding men, victorious, finder of light, well-sacrificing, well-praised, and self-reliant;
he is the kinsman of the earth, the celebrated progenitor of the sun. 79.
The six sons of Ṣaṇḍikā were Smṛti, Dhiṣaṇā, Vṛṣaparvan, Vṛṣantama, Sādhāraṇa, Sukharatha, Svaśva, Satrājit, and Adbhuta. (80)

The eldest king, the giver of life, the one who has gone forth, the powerful one who bestows strength, the controller, the ordainer, the all-pervading, the swift, the master of illusion, the ancient one, and the great increaser. 81.
He is the one to be chosen, the conqueror of all, the sovereign lord, the radiant heaven, the one whose wrath is true, the giver of cattle, the newly born, and the shatterer of obstacles. 82.
He who makes the prize-winning steeds swift, the distributor of wealth, the source of riches;
the heroic one, desiring heroes, who wields the thunderbolt, the manly, the radiant one. 83.

The son of Vāja, the source of strength, the lord of strengths, the maker of the path; the protector of the dwelling, the leader of the people, the king of the clans, whose belly is the sacrificial oblation.
He of manifested glory, the bringer of wealth, the slayer of the trembling foe;
Akhaṇḍala of wondrous luster, with his entire army, the liberator. 85.
The wielder of the thunderbolt, the lord of waters, the winner of cattle, the master of kine;
he who encompasses the universe, the gatherer, the one who desires [to give], the father of heaven, whose heart is kind. 86.
Samantu by name, facing many directions, the lord of the great, meditating, the giver of gifts, the far-famed and skillful one. 87.
Possessing wondrous power, the sovereign of heaven, impelled by his own vigor, he who bestows wealth by day—the tenth among the deities, skillful, fiercely energetic, and most resplendent. (88)
Thus ends the eighth hundred [of names].
He who is most bountiful, the protector from distress, whose thought is thus directed, who shines forth, the bold, the impetuous;
he who is difficult to overcome, the unshakable, the measurer of heaven, the bull of heaven. 89.

Worthy of being honored, the slayer of Dasyus, the bold one; the possessor of sacrificial gifts, rich in wisdom; the seeker of wealth, the impetuous one; the ordainer, the compassionate one, the winner of riches. || 90 ||
Divine, doubly mighty, noble, protector in battle, pre-eminent friend, dwelling in heaven, equal [to all], most wondrous, lord of bounty, and irresistible. 91.
Sovereign of the earth, powerful, bestower of vitality, guardian of the cosmic order, and skillful;
he alone rules over those who do not submit, a singular hero with vast conquests. 92.
The creator of the world, the progenitor of horses, the progenitor of cattle, the singer of births, the king, the lover of hymns, and the protector of the one who presses the soma. 93.
Wearing his garment, king of the peoples, worthy of hymns, with handsome jaws, broad, praiseworthy, most bountiful, swift, loud-shouting, and self-possessed. 94.

The wakeful king of the world, the wise one who finds cattle and wealth, the conqueror, the subduer, the one who does not sink, the giver, the destroyer of the Asuras, and the protector of the waters. 95.
Bold, the domestic lord, more powerful than the powerful, infinite, unobstructed, the giver of wealth, the lord of riches, the wise one, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra. 96.
Unassailed, he has come from behind the *śāla* trees; he has been brought forth as a heap of dust on the path.
He stands at the head of the *vohlāva*, possessing manly vigor, possessing virility, like a wolf, [coming] from the well.

The embryo, the peerless one, free from the eightfold [impurities], the yoke-bearer, the radiant, the unassailable, the protector, the one who bestows abundance, the light-maker, and the lord of songs. 98.
Thus ends the ninth hundred of names.

Blameless, well-endowed, like the wielder of the thunderbolt, like the wielder of the mountain, radiant, wondrous, worthy of sacrifice, most heroic in battle, a subduer of enemies, and a performer of what is right. 99.
The serpent-like devourer, impelled by the sacred word (*brahman*), is Yama;
he stands firm in praise, the shatterer of fortresses, the kinsman who dwells in the vast heaven. 100.
The protector of honey, the king, the leader, the far-extending youth;
he of wide renown, the hearer of our call, the giver of much, possessed of great glory. 101.
He is the father of the streams, the bull, the great giver, the great slayer;
he is easy to approach, the bestower of wealth, the ever-conquering one, and the roaring river among the waters. 102.
He who withholds desire, the winner of light, the most gracious one, strengthened by power;
the priest of the dwelling, the bull of the rivers, the enjoyer, the best of charioteers. 103.
The friend of the sages, the progenitor, the self-dependent, the peerless and irresistible; the wise one, the sacrifice, the mortal, the one of vast hymns, the protector, and Bhaga. 104.
The unconquerable one, the subduer of enemies, the upholder, the hero, the doer, the lord of the people;
the one to be invoked from of old, the protector of the one who has come for refuge;
the well-praised, the immortal, the unassailable, the stirrer of the battle-drum, the giver of strength and of wealth. 106.
Amatra is Mitra, who is to be invoked; Sudāmā is Mahīmahī;
Rathas is Subāhu; Uśanas is Sunītha; Bhūridā is Sudās. || 107 ||
The king of intoxication, having drunk of Soma, is the lord of heaven; he is powerful, wealthy, a warrior, one who hears the invocation, victorious, and a self-ruling sovereign.
Thus ends the tenth century of names.
In this regard, there are these summary verses:
This thousand names of Indra, supremely purifying, Gaṇapati has compiled and bound together from the Ṛgveda. || 1 ||
In this [work], there is no redundancy of names, nor is there the insertion of particles such as "ca" for the sake of filling out the meter;
furthermore, the conclusion of the hundred [stanzas] does not occur in the middle of a verse. (2)
Since these names are Vedic in nature, the learned should examine them all according to their metrical form to ensure the purity of the words.
The various names [of the deities] are to be employed in worship;
they are used in the dative case endings according to their respective order and sequence.
The full fruit that is obtained from the practice of Vedic study should be known to belong to the service of this Thousand Names, which is rooted in the Vedas.
This thousand-name collection is the essence extracted from the mantras;
for him who worships this [collection] belonging to Indra with devotion, the supernatural powers (siddhis) shall come under his control.
The divine Indra, the lord of the entire world, is victorious;
he conquers this very thing by means of his thousand names, which have the Veda as their root. (7)
Thus ends the *Indrasahasranāmastotra*, the work of Gaṇapati, son of Narasiṃha and disciple of the venerable great sage Ramaṇa, belonging to the lineage of Vasiṣṭha.
